title: MergeApproval FK Lifecycle Fix & Safety Validation

chosen_fk_design.label: Remove LoserPaperID's foreign key entirely
chosen_fk_design.loser_paper_id_on_delete: no FK constraint at all (Phase 4K.1 change)

rejected_alternatives.label: LoserPaperID ON DELETE SET NULL
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: Silently destroys the loser's real identity from the column at exactly the moment (post-merge) it matters most; only indirectly reconstructable via ExecutionAuditLogID -> AuditLog.TargetID, and only for EXECUTED rows

rejected_alternatives.label: Both SurvivorPaperID and LoserPaperID ON DELETE SET NULL
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: Same defect as A, plus removes the survivor's own safety-net protection for no offsetting benefit

rejected_alternatives.label: LoserPaperID ON DELETE CASCADE
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: Deletes the MergeApproval row itself the instant the loser is deleted, destroying the exact audit trail the table exists to preserve -- directly contradicts the migration's own stated design rationale

live_precedent.directly_analogous: structurally similar, not perfectly identical (TargetID is polymorphic via TargetType; LoserPaperID is monomorphic)
live_precedent.used_as: evidence that dropping the FK is a safe, already-in-production pattern in this exact schema

migration_change.diff_summary: LoserPaperID INT NOT NULL REFERENCES "ResearchPaper"("PaperID") ON DELETE NO ACTION  ->  LoserPaperID INT NOT NULL

database_level_validation_method.reason: no local psql/postgres binary found; no second, non-production database configured in .env; production is read-only for this phase
database_level_validation_method.simulation_mechanism: ExecutorFakeCursor.enforce_loser_paper_id_fk -- encodes PostgreSQL's real, documented, undeferred ON DELETE NO ACTION semantics directly (a DELETE against a row referenced by such a constraint fails immediately if a referencing row exists)
database_level_validation_method.faithfulness_proof: the simulation was first used to reproduce the exact Phase 4K failure under the original schema, before being used to prove the corrected schema removes it -- not merely asserted to work
cannot_prove: DEFERRABLE constraint timing under concurrent load
database_level_validation_method.recommended_stronger_validation: apply the corrected migration once against a real disposable/staging PostgreSQL instance (or via apply_migration.py --dry-run's real-SQL-then-rollback capability) and confirm a real DELETE succeeds, before ever applying it to production

test_classes.name: OriginalDesignReproducesThePhase4KFailure
test_classes.proves: the exact Phase 4K failure mode reproduces under the original schema, and leaves zero partial corruption on failure

test_classes.name: CorrectedDesignSucceeds
test_classes.proves: the corrected schema allows the full approve -> execute -> EXECUTED lifecycle to complete, with the merged pair's historical identity directly and independently recoverable

executor_order_recheck.sequence: merge_group() [remaps -> AuditLog -> loser DELETE] -> MergeApproval EXECUTED update -> (caller) commit
executor_order_recheck.classification_reasoning: Exception propagation / no-internal-commit discipline is real and tested (Phase 4J's M/N/O/P, re-run unchanged, 39/39 passing); no real caller wraps execute_approved_merge() in a transaction anywhere in the repository yet (grep confirms only merge_executor.py and its own tests reference it)

auditlog_userid_hardcoded_null.must_fix_before: any general, unsupervised, multi-user production rollout
auditlog_userid_hardcoded_null.acceptable_for: a single, human-supervised canary execution, where the operator is externally identifiable

tenant_scoping_absent_in_has_litrix_perm.location: accounts/models.py::User.get_permissions() -- no TenantID clause in its query
tenant_scoping_absent_in_has_litrix_perm.reason_not_blocking_for_canary: both ResearchPaper rows (5232, 5482) share TenantID=1, live-reconfirmed this phase

test_merge_executor.py.note: gained an opt-in, default-off FK-simulation flag with zero behavioral change to existing tests
